# Otar the Foul

|             |                                                        |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Species** | Red Slaad (aberration) — *Otar*, OH-tar, Slaad-tongue root, guttural and blunt |
| **Role**    | Primary-chamber boss, Calveno — Beffa Grung Raid |
| **Location**| [[calveno-sewers-grung-magazines|Calveno Sewer Magazines]], primary detonation chamber, Mercatura collector system |

Not a nameless Red Slaad pulled from Limbo at random — among the few planar scholars who catalogue individual slaadi, this one has a name: Otar the Foul. He manifests through [[solange-barret|Solange Barret]]'s body: a shadow pools at her feet, forms into jaws that close around her, then coats her red skin as a thick black ichor. Her body transforms violently over two to three seconds — she is consumed, not killed, not possessed. What stands in the circle afterward is Otar, wearing flesh that was hers and is now his. The transformation cannot be reversed.

From inside the primary chamber, witnesses see the full body horror. From the surface, civilians see only the result: the Mercatura plaza collapsing and something massive, red, and toad-like hauling itself out of the crater. His hide is cracked and perpetually mid-molt, weeping iridescent fluid; sickly green miasma curls from the splits in his skin. He looks ancient and rotting — a metamorphosis that started centuries ago and never finished.

Otar is a red slaad whose caste transformation (red → blue → green → grey) stalled centuries ago. He stayed red, and he rotted — the foulness is literal, a byproduct of the stalled metamorphosis. No control gem, no binding, no leash: [[simone-tabarnack|Simone]]'s summoning circle was keyed to his specific resonance using techniques the Grung did not develop themselves. The contractor who built the circle knew exactly what they were summoning; that contractor's identity is an open investigation hook.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Recalibration (post-Session 04).** The party combat primer (legacy
> source, migrated R32 as per-PC Arc Notes — no single wiki page for this
> fact) confirms the party punches ~1–2 CR above standard math — coordinated
> focus fire, save-stacking (Bardic Inspiration), and grapple lockdown have
> made every fight through Session 04 land soft. The original CR 8 build
> undertuned that gap; rebuilt to CR 12 (AC 17, HP 241, +11 to hit, DC 17
> saves, 3 legendary actions/round, Legendary Resistance 3/day — up from 1,
> since a single failed save no longer ends the fight against Stunning
> Strike + an established grapple-lockdown pattern). This also has to
> absorb [[catarina-davirelli|Catarina]]'s kit being active from round 1
> even though she personally is 2–3 turns out — see below.

**Design intent:** Foul Miasma taxes melee range (2d6 poison/turn) without punishing ranged parties, which is why Tongue Lash (30-ft grapple + pull) exists — it specifically counters ranged kiting. Entropic Regeneration (12 HP/round, suppressed only by fire or acid) demands sustained pressure so the party can't burst him in two rounds and move on. Chaos Pulse punishes clustering. Legendary actions are reflexive, not tactical — Lash pulls someone in, Thrash clears melee, Bile Spray punishes clustering, all unintelligent. Lair actions represent the unstable plaza, not Otar's own cunning. The fight is meant to feel like containing a disaster, not outmaneuvering a commander — every round spent on Otar is a round the extraction at the four secondary sites runs unopposed. The real boss is the clock.

**Behavioral profile:** Opens by standing where Solange was — disoriented, newly embodied — and Tongue Lashes the nearest visible creature to pull it into melee, then closes; opens with Chaos Pulse instead if 3+ creatures cluster within 20 ft. At 120 HP (half), Unstable Form activates. Otar has no morale: does not retreat, surrender, or reason, and fights until dead. Role: brute/hazard, chaotic — an obstacle, not an opponent.

**Weakness — fire/acid:** suppressing the 12 HP/round regeneration is the tactical key; at 241 HP, without it the party is fighting a wall that heals back most of a round's damage every round. Otar's own Bile Spray deals acid — if it splashes a PC standing near him, that suppresses his own regen; he's too dumb to avoid this. [[catarina-davirelli|Catarina]]'s Wand of Pyrotechnics is a fire source the moment she's in range. With fire suppressing regen early, the fight runs 6–7 rounds; without it, 8+.

**Civilians:** 2d6 injured civilians are trapped in rubble within 30 ft of the crater at the start of combat. Otar attacks them if no PC is within reach (d6 per adjacent round, 1–2 he targets the civilian). Foul Miasma affects them too.

**The clock:** every round at the Mercatura is a round the extraction runs at the four secondary sites. After round 3, screams are audible from the Bridge district (a second strike point active); after round 5, smoke is visible from [[le-paludi|Le Paludi]]. The party must decide whether to finish Otar or split to save people.

**Scaling:** if the fight runs too easy, Otar targets a civilian cluster to force repositioning rather than let the party focus-fire, or Tongue Lashes a PC into the crater for bad positioning. If the party splits early, he pursues the nearest target for 2 rounds, then loses interest and turns on civilians — chaos, not strategy. If the party still has Heroes' Feast active (skipped the long rest), the buffer is significant and the Rattle (below) is less likely to trigger.

**Death:** when Otar dies, all lair actions cease — his and the Rattle's both. He does not dissolve; he falls, bleeding iridescent fluid into the rubble, thirty feet of dead outsider cooling in the middle of a Tessarine commercial plaza. The summoning circle beneath the rubble stays faintly visible. Someone brought this thing here on purpose, and they knew its name.

**Encounter adaptation — Catarina's kit:** [[catarina-davirelli|Catarina]] is introduced earlier in Session 06 and normally joins the party before the primary chamber, a full 5th PC from turn 1. (Fallback only, if the party reaches Room 8 before she's introduced: her cannon and owl are on-site and active from round 1 while she is 2–3 turns of movement out; the DM introduces her before Room 8 by default.) Her Eldritch Cannon ("Ragnetto") and clockwork owl ("Strix") — full stats and behavior already live on [[catarina-davirelli|Catarina]]'s own page — never target Jean-Claude, and raise Otar's effective target CR from turn 1 even though Catarina's body isn't there yet; the CR 12 rebuild above already prices this in.

## Stats & Combat

**Lair actions — the shattered plaza.** Not controlled by Otar; the ground is falling apart. On initiative count 20 (losing ties), one occurs (never the same effect two rounds running):

- **Aftershock.** Each creature on the ground within 15 ft of the crater
  edge: DC 15 Dex save or fall prone.
- **Choking Dust.** A 15-ft-radius sphere becomes heavily obscured until
  initiative count 20 of the next round.
- **Masonry Collapse.** One creature within 40 ft (DM's choice): DC 15 Dex
  save or take 11 (3d6) bludgeoning and be restrained by rubble (escape DC 15, or an ally frees them with an action).

**The Rattle — the [[warren|Warren]] fights beside you.** The Warren's own alarm/mutual-aid system (see that page for the general mechanic), expressed here as action economy: when the fight tips toward a TPK, the party gains its own lair action and a shared legendary-action pool, mirroring Otar. **Trigger:** two PCs unconscious at once, OR party aggregate HP below 25%, OR the DM reads a forming TPK — starts on initiative 20 the following round, lasts until Otar falls. Does not kill Otar; buys room to finish him. Party lair action (initiative 20, right after Otar's, DM or party picks, no repeats two rounds running): **Human Chain** (frees one prone/buried/ restrained/grappled PC, half speed toward the crater edge, no opportunity attacks — [[essa-two-tooth|Essa Two-Tooth]]'s crew clearing a lane); **Fire Brigade** (any PC may add 1d6 fire to one hit until initiative 20 next round, and that hit suppresses Otar's regen until his next turn); **Din of Pans** (Otar: DC 10 Wisdom save or loses one legendary action next round). Party legendary pool: shared pool of 3 (dial to 2 if too strong), one at a time, refreshes on initiative 20 — **[[vault/shattered-sea/npcs/colla|Colla]]'s Toss** (1 action; a potion of healing arcs to one downed/wounded PC within 30 ft: 2d4+2 HP or stabilize); **Shoulder In** (1 action; one PC moves their speed without opportunity attacks, or Dodges); **[[ruk|Ruk]] Wades In** (2 actions; attacks Otar with his own stat block, or grapples/shoves to break a grapple Otar has on a PC). Fire late and once — the last-resort valve, not a pre-empt.
